chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: He narrated to me al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from Ali ibn Mahzar and Abu Ali ibn Rashid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Among the treasures of the knowledge of God, the Exalted, is the completion (of prayers) in four places: The Sanctuary of God, the Exalted; the Sanctuary of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family); the Sanctuary of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him); and the Sanctuary of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both).

The compiler of this book (may God be pleased with him) said: What is meant is that one should intend to stay in their sanctuaries (peace be upon them) for ten days and complete (prayers), and not intend to stay for less than ten days so as to shorten (prayers). And what those of limited insight say is not valid: that one completes (prayers) in these places in all cases.

key_terms.الْإِتْمَامُ: Completion of prayers (performing four rak'ats instead of two)
key_terms.الْقَصْرُ: Shortening of prayers (performing two rak'ats instead of four)

ai.seo_question: When should a traveler perform full prayers instead of shortened prayers in the holy shrines?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these four locations as 'treasuries of God’s knowledge' (makhazin 'ilm Allah), elevating the shrines of the Ahl al-Bayt to the same juridical status as the Kaaba for the ruling of prayer completion (itmam). The compiler’s note clarifies that the default intention is ten days unless specified otherwise, reflecting the Shia principle of certainty (istishab) in ritual practice. This ruling underscores the spiritual centrality of the Imams, linking their physical resting places directly to divine presence and legal dispensation.
